Your Garden Route Event Guide - 1 October Home Submit Event Advertise Contact Us Sign in Subscribe Your Garden Route Event Guide - 1 October Justin 01 Oct 2026 — 10 min read Share Breaking Waves, The Heads, Knysna October opens with a packed fortnight on the Garden Route. Plett's arts festival takes its final bow, Wilderness hands its village over to local artists for four days, Storms River throws an adventure street party, and Oudtshoorn debuts a desert disco under the Karoo stars. Here's what's on from 1 to 14 October. Not subscribed yet? Sign up below for your free weekly garden route event guide Subscribe Email sent! Check your inbox to complete your signup. No spam. Unsubscribe anytime. Mossel Bay Hartenbos Oktoberfest An afternoon of oompah music, German-style food and cold beer at the Hartenbos amphitheatre, raising funds for two local care and retirement homes. Tickets R100. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 14:00 to 22:00 Venue: ATKV Hartenbos Amphitheatre, Hartenbos, Mossel Bay Basket Case: The Ultimate Green Day Experience A high-energy live tribute to Green Day, delivering the punk-rock anthems and attitude that defined a generation. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 20:00 Venue: ReedValley Farm, R327, Mossel Bay Jo Black Live at ReedValley One of Afrikaans music's best-loved voices brings his deep, heartfelt ballads and sing-along favourites to the ReedValley stage. Date: Saturday 10 October Time: 20:00 Venue: ReedValley Farm, R327, Mossel Bay The Amazing Race: Mossel Bay Edition Grab a partner, friend or family member for a day of riddles, challenges and surprises as you race around town. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 08:00 Venue: Diaz Beach, 1 Beach Road, Mossel Bay Garden Route Armwrestling Tournament A double-elimination showdown open to first-timers and seasoned pullers alike. Step up to the table and test your strength. R100 per person. Date: Saturday 10 October Time: 20:30 Venue: Mooiuitsig Restaurant, Klein Brak River, Mossel Bay Masked Ball with André Schwartz Dust off the formal wear and a mask for an elegant evening of Andrew Lloyd Webber favourites, as André Schwartz takes the stage with My Journey with Webber. R450 per person or R4,500 for a table of 10 through iTickets. Date: Friday 2 October Time: 19:00 to 21:00 Venue: Mossel Bay Town Hall, Mossel Bay Classic Film Nights at the Monroe Theatre Two vintage screenings with a light meal included: Hitchcock's Rear Window on Thursday and It Started in Naples on Friday. Dress the era and book a high tea to make an outing of it. R150 per person, booking essential. Date: Thursday 1 and Friday 2 October Time: 18:00 to 20:30 Venue: Monroe Theatre, Marsh Street, Mossel Bay Koeke en Terte Game Show with Timothy Kieswetter The comedian hosts an interactive, laugh-a-minute game show for grown-ups, with lunch available at the hotel to stretch it into a full afternoon. R250 per person, strictly 18 and over. Date: Sunday 4 October Time: 13:00 to 15:00 Venue: Diaz Hotel and Resort, Mossel Bay Misty Valley Oktoberfest The farm's second Oktoberfest brings craft beer, hearty food and live music, ending with a farm dance and live performer from 18:00. Free entry; cashless event. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 09:00 to 23:00 Venue: Misty Valley Farm, Brandwacht, Mossel Bay George Timothy Kieswetter: Tietelogie en Tottiekunde The Afrikaans comedian's brand-new stand-up show plays three nights at the Arts Theatre. Date: Thursday 1 to Saturday 3 October Time: 19:00 Venue: George Arts Theatre, 125 York Street, George Asem: 'n Viering van Lewe, Woord en Musiek An intimate Afrikaans evening of poetry, song and new music, with Petronel Baard performing alongside poets Stef Kruger and Hannes Visser as they launch their new collections. Bring a picnic basket; bar available. R200 per person. Date: Friday 2 October Time: 19:00 Venue: Attic Atelier, George Toughest Firefighter Alive Firefighters take on punishing, fire-ground-inspired obstacles in a test of strength and endurance, with a Mini Toughest Firefighter Alive for younger competitors on the Saturday. Date: Thursday 1 to Saturday 3 October Time: All day Venue: Garden Route Mall, George SWD Club Cricket Season Opener The new South Western Districts club season bowls off with a full day of pool matches at three George grounds. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: First balls at 09:00 Venue: Rooirivierrif Sports Ground, Pacaltsdorp Sports Ground and NMU Saasveld Campus, George Monkey Swings Hike: Special Edition An eight-kilometre youth and family hike at the foot of the Outeniquas, taking in the monkey swings, a secret tunnel, the arch dam and a hidden waterfall. Aimed at reasonably fit walkers; wear proper hiking shoes. Entries through Entry Ninja. Date: Monday 5 October Time: 08:00 to 13:00 (check-in from 07:45) Venue: Trail Kiosk at GroundZero, corner of Arbour Road and Camphersdrift Street, George Wilderness Wilderness Arts Festival Four days celebrating local visual art, music, performance and literature, with food and entertainment for the whole family. It spreads from Fairy Knowe Hotel to the backpackers, Milkwood Village, The Square and the old train station, and is open to the public. Date: Thursday 8 to Sunday 11 October Time: 09:00 to 17:00 Venue: Fairy Knowe Hotel, 1 Dumbleton Road, and venues across the village, Wilderness Twilight at Timberlake Vinyl DJs spin retro, folk and reggae while you browse thrift stalls and African baskets, with a craft beer and cocktail garden and an acoustic cocoa chai bar. Free entry. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 16:00 to 20:00 Venue: Timberlake Village, Wilderness Sunday Sessions Live music, pizza and cold beer by the beach to round off the weekend. Free entry. Date: Sundays 4 and 11 October Time: 15:00 Venue: Wilderness Beach House, Wilderness Sedgefield Moonshine Distill Oktoberfest Beer specials, live music, dancing and German-inspired food from mid-afternoon until late. Free entry. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 15:00 until late Venue: Moonshine Diner, Sedgefield Magnificent Movie Music The Carpe Musicam! Concert Orchestra and Choir bring favourite film scores to life in an afternoon concert. R180 per person. Date: Sunday 4 October Time: 15:30 Venue: NG Kerk, Sedgefield Country Sokkie Evening at La Bosca A country sokkie night on the farm, with tickets through Quicket. Date: Saturday 10 October Time: 19:00 Venue: La Bosca, Luna Verde Farm, Barrington Road, Sedgefield Knysna Psyshores Festival Four days of techno, progressive and psychedelic music, art, workshops and camping right on the shores of Buffalo Bay. R900 per person. Date: Thursday 1 to Monday 5 October Time: Gates open 12:00 on Thursday Venue: Buffelskop Caravan Park, Buffalo Bay, Knysna Roan Ash Live Home from Nashville, South African singer-songwriter Roan Ash plays an intimate solo acoustic set of lyric-driven country rock. Date: Friday 2 October Time: 20:00 Venue: Simola Hotel, Country Club and Spa, Knysna Plettenberg Bay Plett Arts Festival: Final Weekend The ten-day festival wraps up with live music and jazz, poetry, film, comedy, workshops and exhibitions across town, including the Community Canvas show at Piesang Valley Civic Hall. Free entry. Date: Until Sunday 4 October Time: From 08:00 daily Venue: Various venues, Plettenberg Bay Garden Route Kids Expo The first edition of this family expo, with entertainment, interactive stands and hands-on activities all day. Adults free, children R60. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 10:00 to 16:00 Venue: Asado Fire Grill, Keurboomstrand, Plettenberg Bay Blithe Spirit The Bitou Amateur Theatrical Society stages Noël Coward's witty ghost comedy, with a gala opening night that includes wine and cheese before curtain up. Gala tickets R350 from Barney's Kiosk at Market Square or Quicket. Date: Tuesday 6 to Saturday 10 October Time: 19:30 (gates 18:30 on gala night) Venue: St Peter's Church, Church Street, Plettenberg Bay Fynbos Land Art Tour A guided Plett Arts Festival walk through the land art installations set into the fynbos landscape. R150 per person. Date: Saturday 3 October Time: 10:00 to 12:30 Venue: Fynbos Nature Reserve, Plettenberg Bay The White House Collection The Plettenberg Bay Arts Association's flagship exhibition, a curated gallery show of established artists and collectable work selected by a panel including curator Barbara Lenhard and fine artist Elize Bezuidenhout. Free entry. Date: Until Sunday 4 October Time: 09:00 to 18:00 daily Venue: The White House Theatre, Plettenberg Bay Community Canvas The open, inclusive counterpart to the White House Collection, with exhibitions, live demonstrations and a market-style atmosphere for artists at every stage. Free entry. Date: Until Sunday 4 October Time: 09:00 to 18:00 daily Venue: Piesang Valley Community Hall, Plettenberg Bay Storms River and Tsitsikamma Tsitsikamma Adventure Fest Storms River village hosts three days of trail running, mountain biking and e-bike rides, a Draadkar Grand Prix, padel at Misty Mountain Reserve, a street market, a fashion show, live music and dancing. Free entry. Date: Friday 2 to Sunday 4 October Time: Opens 15:00 Friday; closing ceremony 12:00 Sunday Venue: Darnell Street, Storms River Oudtshoorn Hemelruim A brand-new open-air concert billed as a desert disco under the Klein Karoo stars, with Spoegwolf, Tasché and Oudtshoorn's own Noemwoord. Tickets R295 at Computicket, Checkers, Shoprite and Usave, and cheaper in advance than at the gate. Date: Saturday 10 October Time: Gates 17:00, music from 18:00 Venue: Oudtshoorn Sports Grounds (REC), Oudtshoorn Optimum Meiringspoort Half Marathon The 32nd edition of this much-loved road race runs a new circular route through the Middelplaas area after flood damage in the Poort. Choose the 21.1km or 12.5km; walkers welcome, and spectators can catch the finish in De Rust. Date: Saturday 10 October Time: 12.5km starts 07:00, 21.1km starts 07:15 Venue: Finish at the NG Church grounds, De Rust, near Oudtshoorn in partnership with eradio SA eRadio SA - Live from the Garden Route to the World - your digital home for great music, local stories, and engaging conversations. Monday Social Runs – GTR Primary Menu Home GTR Runs Monday Social Runs Thursday GTR Time Trial Weekend Social Runs Garden Route Road Running (GRR) Strides App Trail Maintenance George 6 Peaks FKT Web Site Contact Us Trail Gear Shop Monday social runs The GTR Social runs take place weekly on Mondays at 17:40. The route will always be advertised on the GTR WhatsApp group on the Monday before 12h00. Please join the WhatsApp Group HERE or click the link below. Headlamps are compulsory in the winter months from April to September, as you will finish in the dark. The circular routes are all approximately 8km in length and take between 1-2 hours depending on the number of stops we make. Dogs are welcome, but must be on leash for the entire time of the run as well as before and afterwards. *The owner of the dog takes full responsibility in case the dog causes harm to any person or other animals. GTR can not be held responsible for any incident with animals at our runs.* Fast runners can download the gpx file(if they don’t know the route) and run at their own speed. The other runners can stick with the group, where we wait for everyone at the main junctions. Nobody will be left behind. We ask that you always listen to the GTR guide and be patient. This is not a race, it’s a run to socialize and enjoy nature. You run at your own risk, GTR is not responsible for your safety in any way or form. Please don’t attend any of our runs if you have any flu or covid like symptoms. We suggest you always run with a backpack with the minimum emergency gear when spending a day out in the mountains. For route descriptions and trail names please refer to https://www.trailforks.com/ You can download the app to your phone. See you there! Celebrating our Community Centre’s first birthday It hardly seems possible that a whole year has passed since Kingswood’s Community Centre and Clubhouse officially opened its doors. By Beatrice Esterhuysen - 23 Sep 2026 Home News The big ONE! Celebrating our Community Centre’s first birthday Advertisement 3 min read Last week, homeowners gathered to celebrate its first birthday, and what better way to mark the occasion than with good company, great music, delicious treats and a little bubbly? As the sun set over the Outeniqua Mountains, it was clear that this was about more than celebrating a building. It was about celebrating the people who made it possible, and the community that has made it come alive. Kingswood homeowners certainly showed up for the occasion, filling the centre with laughter, conversation, dancing, and plenty of good cheer. With music by Suzi Leigh and Glynn Storm (who also entertained us with the opening of the Community Centre one year ago), delicious snacks, and bubbly flowing, it was a lovely evening of catching up with friends, meeting neighbours and simply enjoying being together. Willem Jacobs opens the celebrations This is what happens when a community comes together and makes a space truly its own. If the first birthday is anything to go by, our Community Centre has many more good times, great gatherings and happy memories ahead! The journey to this point was a long one. The Community Centre and Clubhouse was one of the most significant development projects ever undertaken at Kingswood, with construction becoming a familiar sight to residents as the vision gradually took shape. The facility, by way of a special levy, was financed entirely by Kingswood homeowners, making it a truly community-driven investment in the future of the estate. When the doors opened on 1 September 2025, Kingswood gained far more than a new clubhouse. The state-of-the-art facility brought together La Famiglia restaurant, the golf Pro Shop, golfers’ bar and lounge, halfway house, outdoor patio, children’s play area, and flexible spaces for functions and community events. Designed to embrace its spectacular natural surroundings, the centre has quickly become a focal point for both residents and golfers. And what a first year it has been. From family gatherings and celebrations to events, dinners, community activities and simply meeting friends for a coffee or a meal, the centre has become an integral part of everyday Kingswood life. It has given us a place to connect, celebrate, relax and enjoy being part of this community. Advertisement Perhaps that is the greatest achievement of all. A building can be beautifully designed, but it is the people who give it meaning. Happy first birthday to our Community Centre and Clubhouse! Here’s to many more years of bringing Kingswood together. All event photos are by Sanjay Lalwani Suzi Leigh and Glynn Storm Save the Dates There’s plenty to look forward to at Kingswood. On 10 October at 08:00, we’re launching the very first Kingswood Spring Fun Run/Walk – and we hope it will become an annual Kingswood tradition! Bloom & Zoom! Dress in your brightest spring colours, florals or your favourite flower-inspired outfit. Dressing up is optional, but definitely encouraged – and we will have a prize for our best-dressed participant! Bring a friend, bring the kids and, if your four-legged family member wants to join the fun, bring one dog on a leash. Most importantly, come along for a morning of fresh air, fun and community spirit, while helping us raise funds for PDSA George. Let’s make our first Spring Fun Run one to remember! Then, on 4 December, we’ll gather on the grass in front of the Community Centre for Carols by Candlelight. Bring your picnic blanket, pack a picnic, and settle in for a festive evening as Carpe Musicam entertains us and leads us in all our favourite Christmas carols. A beautiful way to celebrate the season and enjoy some good old-fashioned Kingswood community spirit! Photo: George Photography Club ENTERTAINMENT NEWS - Georgians can pick and choose their weekend entertainment from a large variety of events. Below is our weekly calendar for the arts: Eyes on arts. These entries are sent to George Herald on a weekly basis. Have a look and book your tickets for some stunning entertainment on your doorstep. 28 October-7 November | Chicago: The Musical The George Society of Arts presents Chicago: The Musical at the George Arts Theatre. Set in the roaring 1920s, this award-winning musical follows Roxie Hart and Velma Kelly as they compete for fame and headlines. Performances start at 19:00. Tickets are R170-R200 on Webtickets. Parental guidance advised for under-16s. 6 November | Life Community Services celebrates 25 years Life Community Services invites the public to its 25th anniversary celebration at Eden Church, Kraaibosch, on Friday 6 November. Arrival is at 17:30 for 18:00. Tickets are R495 per person. Formal or semi-formal dress. 13-14 November | Three in One - Journey to Self Calindo Productions presents Three in One, the powerful finale of the Journey series, exploring family conflict, forgiveness, faith and healing through Biblical stories.  The production, featuring adult themes, takes place at the Market Community Theatre in George on Friday 13 November at 18:30 and Saturday 14 November at 12:00 and 15:00. Tickets on Webtickets. More information at www.calindo.co.za. 21 November | Live Jazz - One Night Only Enjoy an evening of warm melodies and live jazz featuring vocalist Elrine Lottino, drummer Annemie Nel, pianist Ramon Alexander and bassist Renaldo Hendriks at The Market Community Theatre in George. The performance starts at 18:30. Entrance is R150 per person. Tickets are available on Quicket. Enquiries: 072 369 3304. 29 November - 13 December | Carpe Musicam! Christmas Concerts Carpe Musicam! presents five festive concerts across the Garden Route.  The Carpe Musicam Pops Band will present Sounds of the Season at the Dias Maritime Museum in Mossel Bay on 29 November and Kingswood Golf Estate in George on 4 December, featuring carol singing with “Barefoot” Bea Esterhuizen. The Concert Orchestra and Choir present O Holy Night in Sedgefield on 6 December at 15:30, Hoërskool Outeniqua in George on 11 December at 19:00, and Mossel Bay Town Hall on 13 December at 18:00. Tickets and details at www.carpemusicam.co.za. 29 November - 13 December | Carpe Musicam! Christmas Concerts 11 December | The Music of Bee Gees and Friends Enjoy an evening of nostalgic hits as Vernon Ericson Barnard brings the music of the Bee Gees and friends to life at The Market Community Theatre in George. The show starts at 19:00, with doors opening at 18:00. Tickets cost R120 per person. Enquiries and bookings: Heather on 072 369 3304. • Send details of your cultural events to [email protected] • Send details of your cultural events to [email protected] . 05:00 Max Allowed Race Time 25 Hours Overview Course GENERAL REGISTRATION NOW OPEN This route boasts everything from big climbs, rocky trails, technical downhills, some run-able sections and views of the Outeniqua Mountain Range, secret indigenous forests that will keep your endorphins going on this 100km mountain ultra-trail. You will start with the old Voortrekker pass aka; Cradock pass consisting of the biggest climb of the route. From here you will dip down into the famous Pass to Pass route and cross the Outeniquas into Champherskloof. Here you will experience the fynbos of the Klein Karoo and of course, the heat! Next up a welcoming stop on the famous Montagu Pass before you start your ascent over the mountains again. Your lunch stop might come back to haunt you as you negotiate Dizzy Heights Climb to the top. On the top, you will encounter some of the most sublime mountain running to be had in the Garden Route with 360˚ views all the way down to the George Dam. From here you will cross the mighty Kaaimans river to the Groenkop Nature Reserve. You will enter the picturesque Groeneweide Trails to exit the indigenous forest at Saasveld. From the Saasveld aid station you will run along the banks of the Garden Route Dam to make your way back up to Tierkop where you will re-join the 60km route to make sure you do not miss out on the favourites like The Wall and Tonnelbos. The last few kilometers will include lush forest trails and the cheering point which is Trail Kiosk. Traversing under bridges in the city will lead you to the finish of what is a brutal, yet phenomenal course. GEORGE NEWS - The Transnet Transport Museum temporarily reopened on Saturday 27 June for a well-known local flea market that will continue until Sunday 12 July. For this event, the Powervan has also returned to its usual departure point at the museum. Charl Marais, its operator, said they are grateful to be back, although only temporarily. The museum had been closed since May, when an outside section of the building was damaged by the severe weather. It has since emerged that some areas inside the facility also require urgent maintenance and repairs, which was part of the reason for the closure. Responding to a query from the newspaper, Transnet said on Friday 26 June: “The phased reopening of the Transnet Transport Museum has been undertaken as a considered and negotiated response to requests from tenants and stakeholders, allowing for limited public access while existing safety constraints continue to be managed.  "This arrangement is structured as a temporary concession, with tenants having signed indemnity agreements and undertaken to secure appropriate third-party insurance as part of the conditions for operating within the facility. While the museum is currently accessible on a limited basis, any continuation beyond 12 July will remain subject to ongoing risk assessments and strict compliance with safety requirements. “Progress has been made in addressing certain repairs within the building, however, further remedial work remains dependent on internal governance processes, including the finalisation of budgets and procurement approvals. Transnet continues to engage internally to ensure that priority infrastructure and safety concerns are addressed in a structured and compliant manner.” Transnet said at this stage, it is not possible to confirm a date for the full reopening of the museum.  The timeline will depend on the completion of outstanding repairs, the appointment of the necessary contractors and the implementation of a comprehensive maintenance plan. Pieter du Plessis, the main organiser of the flea market (The Market @ Transnet Transport Museum), said significant time and investment had gone into organising the event, and they are relieved that it can take place. The Transnet Transport Museum is currently open until 12 July. Let's Love Local Gift Market | George | Christmas Market - Let's Love Local Skip to main content Now preparing our next market Home About us Instagram Feed Gallery Next Market Applications Testimonials FAQ's Contact Us Let's Love Local   Gift Market Menu about   Us Loving Local since 2015 Founded in 2015, Let’s Love Local Gift Market in George is one of South Africa’s largest holiday markets, showcasing over 220 vendors from across the country. As a premier Garden Route Christmas Market, we offer a boutique holiday shopping experience filled with handmade South African gifts, artisanal home decor, and unique local crafts. Proudly hosted by Boerevintage (Pty) Ltd , the event maintains the same high-quality standards and welcoming atmosphere our visitors have loved for years. Held each December in a spacious marquee at Redberry Farm , the market is a cornerstone of the community, supporting small businesses, employing 50 locals, and sourcing 90% of our services within the region. Endorsed by George Tourism, we are a must-visit destination for both residents and tourists. If you are looking for the best things to do in George in December or searching for the ultimate Christmas market in the Garden Route, join us at Redberry Farm for an unforgettable festive experience. our Instagram Feed our Gift Market Gallery next Let's Love Local Gift Market starting in DATES & TIMES: 12 December 2026 - 2 January 2027 Open Monday - Saturday (9am - 4pm), CLOSED on Sundays and Christmas Day. Frequently asked Questions vendor Applications Our vendor application window period is normally open between 1 March and 30 April each year.  This period is now closed and our 2026 vendors have been selected. You may still contact us if you would like more information or would like to discuss possible participation in our market. Click the link below to make contact with us. Any other enquiries?     Use the contact Us form and we'll get back to you! our Testimonials The market has a 4.8/5 ⭐ on Google from 153 reviews. Here are some highlights...   Monique   Lingenfelder " BoereVintage – Let’s Love Local Gift Market is honestly one of my absolute favourite places to browse and shop! I love how many different types of products there are – you can find a little bit of everything and it always feels so special and proudly local. My personal favourites are definitely the Meelbroeke stall 😍 and the amazing stall that sells the b-earth products – I always end up going back there! Such a warm, creative and happy market to visit. Highly recommend! " Kristel van Heerden " Great market. A must visit during the December Holidays. My favorite market across the whole garden route by far. Such great variety. Bring all your friends and family and support all the local vendors. I have visited multiple times this year alone and everytime I see new things I want to buy. I have supported this market for about 10 years now and every year it just seems to grow bigger and better " Janine Victor "There are very few places that I can drag my husband to with no kicking and screaming. He actually even bought Christmas gifts, including one for me. I did most of my shopping for my family at this market because I found a large variety of unique, useful and well-priced gifts. These included jewellery, coasters, clothes, body butter with a divine fenjal scent, beeswax products, beautiful ceramics, attractive fire lighters, leather braai gloves, lots of heavenly scented stuff and if you are still reading be sure to go." Marisha Vollmeyer " 10/10 One of the best markets in the Garden Route to attend. It is hard to not want to go everyday! A lovely experience for the whole family filled with so much creativity and inspiring vendors. " our Gift Market FAQ'S FAQ’s Where is Let's Love Local Gift Market located? The market is proudly hosted at Redberry Farm in George , located on Geelhoutboom Road, Blanco. It is the perfect destination for families visiting the Garden Route during the December holidays, offering a festive atmosphere right at the foot of the Outeniqua Mountains. Find us on the map here What are the market dates and opening hours for 2026? For the 2026 festive season, the market will be open from 12 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 . We are open Monday to Saturday from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm . Please note that the market is closed on Sundays and Christmas Day , in line with Redberry Farm's operating hours. Is there an entrance fee for the market? No, entrance to Boerevintage Let's Love Local Gift Market is completely free! We welcome all residents and holiday visitors to browse our 220+ artisanal stalls at no cost. Please note that while the market is free, other activities at Redberry Farm (like strawberry picking or the hedge maze) may have their own separate fees. Is the market pet-friendly? Because Redberry Farm is a working commercial farm with strict bio-hazard and safety rules, no pets are allowed on the premises, including small pets carried in bags. We appreciate your understanding in helping us maintain the farm's high standards. Is the market accessible for wheelchairs and prams? Yes! Let’s Love Local Gift Market is held in a large marquee on a well-maintained, level grass field. To ensure a comfortable experience, we have installed 1.6-metre wide aisles throughout the market. All aisles are covered with PVC walkway runners , providing a stable and smooth path for wheelchairs, mobility aids, trolleys, and prams to navigate easily. How do I become a vendor at Let's Love Local Gift Market? We welcome creative entrepreneurs and artisans from all over South Africa ! While we are based in George, our mission is to support "local" on a national scale. Applications for our 2026 festive market open on 1 March 2026 and close on 30 April 2026 . During this window, you can download the application pack from our Applications section. If you produce high-quality, South African-made products, we invite you to apply to be part of this beloved holiday tradition. Can't wait for December? Follow us for vendor sneak peeks and market news! Kevin Fraser Official Website Welcome to DECADANCE — a comedy celebration marking 10 years of Kevin Fraser on stage. Born in 1990, Kevin’s story as an entertainer took an unlikely turn in 2016, when he began filming outrageous accents and characters from a humble container shed in Tasmania, Australia. Those viral videos sparked a journey that moved from small Aussie shows to stages across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and beyond. Each year added new chapters: Australia in 2016, more countries joining in 2017, a global explosion by 2018, and a steady climb through 2019, 2020, 2021… all the way to 2025 — with every tour, every city, and every character shaping the phenomenon Kevin is today. Now, in 2026, Kevin rewinds the clock to bring fans the ultimate throwback party: a decade of chaos, culture, and comedy reimagined for the stage. Expect the nineties nostalgia that shaped him, the container-shed characters that started it all, and the world-travelled stories that turned everyday madness into global punchlines. This isn’t just a comedy show — it’s a time capsule cracked open, a decade of laughs uncorked, and an invitation to dance through Kevin’s first ten years in comedy. Built around authentic acoustic instrumentation — tin guitar, banjo, mandolin, violin, harmonica and accordion — the band draws deeply on Cape Malay and traditional Afrikaans musical roots while pushing them into unexpected new territory. Since their debut, the Orkes have released a string of acclaimed albums, including Stoomradio, Die Nagloper, Opgestook, Heuningland and Mamba, and have shared stages and studios with artists such as Chris Chameleon, Valiant Swart and Jack Parow, with lyrics and songwriting contributions from renowned author Rian Malan. Equal parts theatre, storytelling and music, a Radio Kalahari Orkes performance is a singular South African experience — and demand for the band continues to grow. Hear Schumann’s Fantasiestücke, Schubert’s songlike Impromptu, and Liszt’s dazzling Rigoletto paraphrase, a four-voice opera quartet reimagined at the keyboard. Discover Mel Bonis’s charming “Gai Printemps,” then let the clarinet find its blues, klezmer and Latin soul in works by Mangani, Kovács and Paquito D’Rivera. There’s Malcolm Arnold’s swaggering Sonatina, and Hendrik Hofmeyr’s sombre Canto Notturno from South Africa’s own composing voice. Classical, jazz, klezmer and more, all in one programme. Join us at 6.30 before the concert for a glass of complimentary bubbles to celebrate the year. Big character. We're an independent, family-run microbrewery — no suits, no shortcuts. The original brewery fired up in 2013, and we’ve been running the show since 2019, pouring everything into brewing bold, no-nonsense beer the way it should be made: from grain to glass, by hand. We don’t mess with preservatives or major filtration. Instead, we let gravity do the work, pulling out most of the yeast while leaving just enough behind to punch up the body and bring serious flavour. It’s raw, it’s real, and it’s brewed on a proudly South African-built system. Every single batch is hands-on: from mashing the grain to carbonating our kegs — hell, we even label every can one by one. No machines, no mass production, just pure dedication. Our name comes from Knysna’s iconic Red Bridge —  a 100-year-old legend and local hideaway where locals cycle, swim, walk their dogs, and sip sundowners. It’s got history. Just like our beer. The Red Bridge Opened in 1923 this is the third bridge to span the Knysna River. Originally built for local traffic the bridge is now closed to vehicles and has instead become a popular exercise route, mountain bike route, dog walking haven and picnic stop. Most of the locals also enjoy a bit of an adrenaline thrill by jumping off the bridge into the river. One of the great spots to watch the African sunset with a few cold beers & great friends. Your Garden Route Event Guide - 8 October Home Submit Event Advertise Contact Us Sign in Subscribe Your Garden Route Event Guide - 8 October Justin 08 Oct 2026 — 9 min read Share ‎⁨Coney Glen Beach⁩, ⁨Knysna⁩ Highlights this week include Hemelruim's first desert disco in Oudtshoorn, the tenth Garden Route Kite Festival in Sedgefield, the Fancourt Marathon in George, the Topper Nationals in Mossel Bay and the Plett Games. Not subscribed yet? Sign up below for your free weekly garden route event guide Subscribe Email sent! Check your inbox to complete your signup. No spam. Unsubscribe anytime. Mossel Bay Tanja Storm: Ballads and Blues Tanja Storm performs an evening of ballads and blues with guest Blackie Swart at this Little Brak River music venue. Date:  Wednesday 7 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  Blou Kombuis, 2nd Avenue, Little Brak River, Mossel Bay Moss March A community walk with purpose on the Hartenbos seafront, part of the Mossel Bay Sport and Recreation Festival. Entry is free; walkers are asked to bring tinned or non-perishable food and socks for those in need. Strongman and powerlifting competitions follow at the same venue. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  07:00 to 09:00 Venue:  Hartenbos Seefront, 156 Paardekraal Avenue, Hartenbos, Mossel Bay Garden Route Armwrestling Tournament A double-elimination showdown open to first-timers and seasoned pullers alike. Entry is R100 for one arm or R150 for both, and spectator tickets cost R100. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  Registration and weigh-ins from 08:30, tournament from 10:00 Venue:  Mooiuitsig Restaurant, Brinkley's River Village, 1 Old George Road, Klein Brak River, Mossel Bay Misty Valley Oktoberfest The farm's second Oktoberfest runs every Saturday in October with craft beer, food and live music. Entrance is free and the day is cashless. Date:  Saturday 10 October and Saturday 17 October Time:  09:00 to 18:00 Venue:  Misty Valley Farm, R328, Brandwacht, Mossel Bay Jo Black Live at ReedValley An evening of Afrikaans music from Jo Black on the wine estate, with ReedValley wines and food on sale. Tickets start at R220. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  20:00 Venue:  ReedValley Farm, R327, Mossel Bay Magnificent Movie Music Carpe Musicam brings its programme of orchestral and choral film favourites to the Town Hall for a 90-minute Sunday afternoon concert, with violinist Marie-Jean Kotzé as soloist. Tickets cost R180 for adults and R60 for scholars from carpemusicam.co.za. Date:  Sunday 11 October Time:  15:30 Venue:  Mossel Bay Town Hall, 101 Marsh Street, Mossel Bay Song Sung Blue at The Blue Shed Open Plan Pictures screens Song Sung Blue, the story of two down-on-their-luck performers who form a Neil Diamond tribute act, as part of its spring movie series. Tickets start at R100. Date:  Friday 16 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  The Blue Shed, 33 Bland Street, Mossel Bay Topper Nationals Mossel Bay Sailing Club and the Skipper Foundation host the national championship for the Topper dinghy class. Spectators are welcome on the beach to watch young sailors race in the bay. Date:  Saturday 17 October and Sunday 18 October Time:  10:00 to 17:00 Venue:  Santos Beach, Santos Road, Mossel Bay George Carpe Musicam: Magnificent Movie Music The Carpe Musicam Concert Orchestra and Choir play a dozen film themes spanning eight decades, from The Sound of Music to The Mission and The Mask of Zorro, with violinist Marie-Jean Kotzé as soloist. Tickets cost R180 for adults and R60 for scholars, with limited sales at the door. Date:  Friday 9 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  Laerskool George-Suid, corner of Meade and Laing Streets, George MRC Rugby Expo Two days of senior men's club rugby, under-19 and under-13 schoolboy rugby, senior ladies' netball and chess, with food vendors, a cash bar and live entertainment. Entry is R50 for adults. Date:  Saturday 10 October and Sunday 11 October Time:  From 09:00 Venue:  Pacaltsdorp Sportgronde, 66 Olympic Street, Pacaltsdorp, George Espectáculo Marlise's School of Spanish Dance presents an evening of Spanish dance. Tickets cost R150 through Webtickets. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  18:30 Venue:  Market Community Theatre, George Sedgefield Country Sokkie Evening at La Bosca Country music and sokkie dancing in the countryside, with a Best Dressed Country Couple competition. The restaurant serves Portuguese and Italian dishes from noon. Tickets cost R80 for adults and R40 for children aged 6 to 12. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  19:00 to 23:00 Venue:  La Bosca, Luna Verde Farm, Barrington Road, Sedgefield Pink Walk for Breast Cancer Awareness A free 4.5 km community walk in pink, with prizes for the best dressed. Donations go to Hospice Sedgefield. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  08:30 Venue:  Engen Garage, Sedgefield Garden Route Kite Festival The tenth RE/MAX Garden Route Kite Festival brings kite flyers and makers from nine countries to Sedgefield. Bring a kite, make one on the day or buy one there. Food stalls, coffee and family entertainment run all day, and entry is free. Date:  Sunday 18 October Time:  09:30 to 15:30 Venue:  Scarab Village, Sedgefield Knysna Schalk Bezuidenhout: Hey Hey Divorce Schalk Bezuidenhout's stand-up show about his own divorce, which he says is cheaper than therapy. Tickets cost R300 with unreserved seating, and doors open at 19:00. Date:  Tuesday 20 October Time:  20:00 Venue:  Simola Hotel Country Club and Spa, Knysna Plettenberg Bay Blithe Spirit The Bitou Amateur Theatrical Society stages Noël Coward's ghost comedy, directed and designed by David Hall-Green. Tuesday is the gala opening, with doors at 18:30 and complimentary wine and cheese. Tickets cost R350 from Barney's Kiosk or Quicket. Date:  Tuesday 6 October to Saturday 10 October Time:  19:30 Venue:  St Peter's Church, Plettenberg Bay Bekkersdal Bachelors and Blunders A one-man evening of Herman Charles Bosman's Oom Schalk Lourens stories, told with dry Groot Marico humour. Tickets are sold through Quicket. Date:  Tuesday 6 October Time:  19:30 Venue:  The White House Theatre, 6 Crescent Street, Plettenberg Bay Plett Games A family festival hosted by Greenwood Bay College. Teams of three to five, or individuals, work through twelve challenges, from gumboot throwing and golf chipping to slow cycling and paper plane contests. The Bitou River Band plays live, with sourdough pizza, a beer garden, a tea garden and children's play areas. Tickets cost R30 to R150. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  10:00 to 17:00 Venue:  Greenwood Bay College, Piesang Valley Road, Plettenberg Bay Oudtshoorn Optimum Meiringspoort Half Marathon The 32nd edition of this much-loved road race offers 21.1 km and 12.5 km distances. After flood damage, runners are now transported out on the Uniondale road (R341) for a run back into De Rust. Entries are sold out, and spectators can catch the finish at the church grounds. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  12.5 km starts 07:00, 21.1 km starts 07:15 Venue:  Finish at the NG Church grounds, De Rust, near Oudtshoorn Hemelruim: Music Under the Stars A new open-air concert from the KKNK, billed as a desert disco under the Klein Karoo sky. Spoegwolf, Tasché and Oudtshoorn's own Noemwoord share the stage. The concert has moved to a new venue, Surval Boutique Olive Estate. Tickets cost R295 through Computicket, and children aged 7 to 13 pay R100 at the gate. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  Gates open at 17:00, music from 18:00 Venue:  Surval Boutique Olive Estate, R328, Oudtshoorn Klein Karoo Dust 4 Glory Challenge An obstacle course race with climbing, crawling, water and mud, part of the OFSA National Series. Distances range from a 1 to 2 km Mini for ages 3 to 10 up to the 12 km Pro with more than 20 obstacles. Entries cost R150 to R550 and are limited. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  Registration 06:00 to 08:00; Medium at 08:00, Pro at 09:00, junior races at 12:00 Venue:  Wilgewandel Holiday Farm, 2 km from the Cango Caves, Oudtshoorn That’s a wrap! It is a monumental race from the dark side of the Swartberg Mountain Range at the Northern slopes in the Great Karoo through the Klein Karoo region towards the northern foothills of the Outeniqua mountains and a finish in the Langkloof at Louvain Guest Farm. The vast landscapes and diverse overload of this non-technical routes are the perfect race for all mountain and gravel bike enthusiasts, with ample opportunity to appreciate the unique surroundings you’ll be exposed to. Steve Newman , one of South Africa's finest musical treasures - his project, Tananas, has played concerts/festivals on nearly all the world’s continents including Asia, Africa, the US, Europe, and Australia. Eugene Van Pletzen , a percussionist, drummer and lover of swung rhythms and the stories they tell and has made a name for himself playing with legendary artists such as Steve Newman and many others. Sip a glass of wine while you enjoy the music and then linger in the gardens or the pavilion and enjoy a 'BYO' picnic lunch. Tables and chairs will be provided. At the same time Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young began writing the songs of an anti-war, anti-establishment, anti-discrimination generation on the other side of the world. Two generations later, Keith's grandsons Nick and Matt Catto, together with Jono Tait, are singing those same songs: Teach Your Children, Our House, Ohio, Helplessly Hoping, Southern Cross. The need for them, it turns out, never really went away. Keith's circle included Des Lindberg and Jeremy Taylor, who was later banned by the apartheid government for his protest songs. South Africa had its own folk revolution playing out in those same years, on a smaller stage, for many of the same reasons. Jono comes from the same lineage. His father, Richard Tait, started out in the folk clubs at UCT and Rhodes in the seventies, chaired the Barleycorn Folk Club committee through the 80s, spent the 90s in bands playing rooms like the Baxter and the National Arts Festival, then opened and ran The Alma Cafe for 21 years, still one of South Africa's best-loved intimate listening venues. Jono, Matt and Nick, recipients of multiple ovation awards from the National Arts Festival in Grahamstown for their original music, are now bringing CSNY's songs to the Garden Route. ***** Sarah: "Really excellent harmonies and fully embodied Crosby Nash Stills and Young. One of the best tribute bands I have seen." ***** Andyjay: "Awesome harmonies, out of this world, and the musos were first class. Great show, brought tears to my eyes." ***** Sue: "The music was so good - I sang my way through all the songs! Especially 'Four Dead In Ohio' transported me right back to my youth. Amazing evening!" ***** Engela: "We absolutely loved the show. It took us right back to when we saw CSN and Y live many years ago. Great harmonies with each member bringing a special touch and talent to the show. One of the best tribute shows I have seen. Highly recommended." Three voices. Acoustic instruments. No theatrics. Just the harmony these musicians have been building for three generations. Bay at The Sanctuary Restaurant Events on the Garden Route A Christmas Feast in the Heart of Plettenberg Bay at The Sanctuary Restaurant Marvin Leugering 3 weeks ago 0 4 mins Summary: The Sanctuary Restaurant at Plett Quarter Hotel in Plettenberg Bay is hosting a family style Christmas Day lunch on 25 December 2026, from 12:30 to 16:00. The feast costs R945 per person , with children under 16 paying R450. It includes canapes, a Harvest Table starter selection, a choice of one plated main course, a festive dessert buffet and a complimentary glass of bubbly on arrival. Christmas on the Garden Route comes with plenty of reasons to gather around the table. On Friday , 25 December 2026, The Sanctuary Restaurant at Plett Quarter Hotel in Plettenberg Bay is serving a family style Christmas lunch, bringing festive favourites together for a leisurely celebration in the heart of town. The lunch runs from 12:30 to 16:00 and begins with a selection of canapes, followed by Harvest Table starters, a plated main course and a festive dessert buffet. Each guest also receives a complimentary glass of bubbly on arrival, giving the celebrations a sparkling start. The festive meal begins with a selection of canapes: Salmon roulade with cucumber and tomato relish Lemon- and herb-marinated mushrooms, peppers, and zucchini , served with truffle oil aioli Beef skewers served with tzatziki Next up is the Harvest Table starter selection, featuring a Selection of Breads and House Salad, Roasted Beetroot and Butternut Salad, Wilted Wild Rocket Salad with Parmesan, Roasted Vegetable Salad, and Traditional Sticky, Crispy Potato and Leek salad. For the plated main course, guests choose one of four dishes: Citrus-Roasted Gammon: Slow-braised gammon infused with orange and thyme, glazed and served with classic dauphinoise potatoes, fine beans, and confit tomatoes Herb-Infused Deboned Leg of Lamb: Tender leg of lamb infused with thyme, rosemary, and teriyaki sauce, served with crispy baby potatoes and seasonal baby root vegetables Roasted Chicken Patissier: Succulent roasted chicken stuffed with a mushroom and thyme ragout, served with crispy potatoes Wholegrain Mustard-Crusted Beef Fillet: Medium-cut fillet medallions served with cauliflower, broccoli, leek gratin, and a rich, creamy red wine jus The festive dessert buffet rounds things off with Famous Baked Cheesecake, Hazelnut Chocolate Brownie served with Mixed Berry Compote, Vanilla Ice Cream, Traditional South African Milk Tart and Cherry Trifle Pudding. With canapes, a generous Harvest Table, a choice of plated main and a dessert buffet, the menu gives Christmas lunch plenty of festive variety. The complimentary glass of bubbly on arrival adds a little sparkle to the start of the meal. The family style Christmas lunch costs R945 per person. Children under 16 pay R450, and every guest receives a complimentary glass of bubbly upon arrival. Reservations are subject to availability and must be secured with full prepayment. Guests are asked to advise of any dietary requirements or food allergies at the time of booking. To enquire or reserve a table, contact The Sanctuary Restaurant at Plett Quarter Hotel on 044 004 0279 or email plettqsanctuary@lionroars.com. Located on Plett’s Main Street, Plett Quarter Hotel & Apartments is in the heart of Plettenberg Bay, making The Sanctuary Restaurant a convenient festive lunch option for locals and holidaymakers spending Christmas in town. For a Christmas Day gathering with a little bubbly, a choice of mains and a dessert buffet to finish, the Plett Quarter feast brings the season to the table. Quick details Event: Family Style Christmas Lunch Restaurant: The Sanctuary Restaurant, Plett Quarter Hotel Location: Main Street, Plettenberg Bay Date: Friday, 25 December 2026 Time: 12:30 to 16:00 Price: R945 per person Children: Under 16 pay R450 Arrival inclusion: Complimentary glass of bubbly per guest Menu: Canapes, Harvest Table starters, one plated main course of choice, festive dessert buffet Booking: Reservations subject to availability, with full prepayment required Dietary requirements: Advise at the time of booking Phone: 044 004 0279 Email: plettqsanctuary@lionroars.com Venue information: https://lionroars.com/lodges/plett-quarter-hotel-apartments Post navigation Previous: Christmas Lunch & Dinner Garden Route 2026 Next: Le Sueur Wines Hosts a Five-Course Pairing Dinner in Knysna at Island Cafe Related News Le Sueur Wines Hosts a Five-Course Pairing Dinner in Knysna at Island Cafe Marvin Leugering 3 weeks ago 0 Enjoy Wine, a Two-Course Lunch and Dessert for R250 in Knysna at Island Cafe Marvin Leugering 1 month ago 0 5 Post House Wines and 5 Courses come to The Turbine in Knysna Marvin Leugering 2 months ago 0 All-You-Can-Eat Prawns and a Heritage Day Seafood Buffet at De Vette Mossel Grootbrak Marvin Leugering 2 months ago 0 Own a Restaurant? Ideal for Families, tourists, locals​ The Sedgefield Mosaic Market is a visual symphony of colours, textures and handcrafted artistry. This is not your typical arts and crafts market; it is the kind of market that will burn a hole in your pocket. Things you didn’t know you needed, and now you can’t live without. Set the trend with your new ispoti hat (contemporary bucket hat), or turn heads with a bright neon tie-dye shirt. Most of what is available at the market was crafted or carefully curated by shop owners. Cliff, with deep roots in the Sedgefield community, is the driving force behind the evolution of the Mosaic Market. His vision and energy have transformed it into a vibrant space for craftspeople, creating a lively atmosphere where creativity thrives and offering a warm welcome to locals and visitors alike every weekend. The Slow Roasted Coffee Shop is your go-to spot for expertly brewed cups made from the finest coffee beans. Whether you’re in the mood for a smooth latte or a creamy cappuccino, the comforting aroma of freshly ground coffee fills the air. Wine lovers are in for a treat at the market’s cosy wine shop, open even on Sundays. It’s the perfect place to restock after your friends or family have enjoyed a little too much of your wine stash the night before. If you’re hungry, the market has a ton of breakfast options. Whether you’re into a big English fry-up, a light pastry, or a healthy smoothie bowl, you’ll find something to hit the spot. Plus, you can enjoy live music in the background while you eat. The Sedgefield Mosaic Market is a treasure trove of unique finds and creative inspiration. Each stall and shop is a testament to local artisans’ and curators’ talent and passion. From handcrafted jewellery to custom artwork, from clothing with a quirky flair to home décor with a touch of magic, there’s something here for everyone. As you wander the market, you’re not just buying things; you’re taking home a piece of the local culture crafted with care and imagination. If you’re planning to visit, arrive early and check out the Wild Oats Community Farmers’ Market , just next door. They close at 12, so it’s a great spot to start your morning with fresh produce and locally-made foods before you head over to the Mosaic Market for more exploring and shopping. Where: 1.5 kilometres west of Sedgefield town, at the Engen Petrol Station. When: Every Saturday morning throughout the year. Time: 8:00 AM – 2:00 AM What sets this market apart: Plenty of colourful and unique artisan gift and crafts Focus on quality local and homemade products. Between them they play more than 8 musical instruments and have over 80 years experience of professional musical performances. “We see it as our joyful duty to pass on our knowledge to anyone who is interested in | improving their musical skills.” Elsabe Barkhuizen Elsabe is a very experienced and sought-after church organist, pianist and harpsichordist who has been playing professionally since the age of 12. Until 2016 she held the post of Director of Music for the Dutch Reformed Church’s Mother Parish in George, South Africa. Her “home” organ was a historic 1879 William Hill of London mechanical pipe-organ. She’s also the co-founder/resident pianist/organist of the Carpe Musicam! Orchestra, a community-based orchestra in the Garden Route. Norman Carless Norman has had a long and successful career in South African military bands and orchestras, being a Bandmaster for the South African Navy before his retirement in 2003. He is a conductor and multi-instrumentalist, performing regularly on the Trumpet, Cornet, Flute, Recorder and the French Horn. He is also a Master Arranger and Orchestrator, specialising in custom orchestrations of popular works for unusual groupings of instruments. In July 2015 he co-founded the Carpe Musicam! Where Barefoot Sophistication Meets Beachside Fun Tucked right on the edge of Myoli Beach , PiliPili Sedgefield is where locals, travellers, and beach lovers gather to eat, sip, surf, and unwind. With toes in the sand and the sound of the ocean in the background, this is more than just a restaurant — it’s a lifestyle. From sunrise coffees to late-night live music, we’re open all day to serve up good times, laid-back vibes, and food that hits the spot. It’s the kind of place you stop by for lunch and end up staying for sunset… or longer. Sedgefield Menu Sedgefield Wine List *MENU PRICE DISCLAIMER: Please note that menu prices are subject to change without prior notice. The prices displayed at the restaurant will always be the final amount charged. While we strive to keep our online and third-party listings up to date, the prices displayed at the restaurant will always be the final amount charged. We are not responsible for outdated menus or pricing uploaded by third parties on platforms such as Google or other websites. For the most current pricing, please refer to our in-house menu or contact the restaurant directly. THE VIBE At PiliPili Sedgefield, every day feels like a beach holiday. Think surfboards, sunsets, live music, spontaneous dancing, and the friendliest crew on the coast. Come as you are — barefoot, salty-haired, and ready for a good time. DRINKS & GOODTIMES Our bar is stocked with local craft beers, icy cocktails, crisp wines, and freshly blended smoothies. Whether you’re kicking back after a swim or toasting with friends under the stars, we’ve got something cold waiting. WHAT'S ON THE MENU? Expect generous portions, fresh ingredients, and global flavours with a PiliPili twist. Wood-fired pizzas, gourmet burgers, seafood specials, and vegetarian favourites — all made fresh and full of flavour. IN-HOUSE ACTIVITIES Myoli Beach is an unspoiled paradise brimming with adventure. At PiliPili, guests can enjoy a variety of in-house activities, including: Paragliding Mountain biking Horse riding Canoeing Beach volleyball STAY WITH US Located just above the PiliPili Beach Restaurant, PiliPili Beach Cabanas offers affordable beachfront accommodation and luxury cabanas for the discerning traveller. From bunk beds for budget adventurers to spacious family rooms, we’ve got the perfect spot for every type BOOK NOW CONVENIENCE SHOP Just around the corner of the PiliPili Sedgefield building, you’ll find our handy little convenience shop — perfect for grabbing everyday essentials or that toothbrush you forgot to pack. We also serve takeaway soft serve ice creams and a great selection of coffees for sit-down or on-the-go. Whether you’re heading to the beach or stocking up for your stay, we’ve got you covered. To celebrate our 10th Anniversary, we honour each person who has participated over the years – and as a gesture of our gratitude we’ve released 70 Tribe Loyalty Tickets (more than twice of what was available last year) at a ridiculously cheap price of R899 – that’s less than R100 per day! So let’s gather again to dance, to sing, to co-create what has become the most unique, magical, family-friendly expression of HEARTISTRY – sharing our gifts and talents from heart to heart, and valuing our own uniqueness as well as the divine light in others. As free spirits, we learn and grow together, we honour the Earth through meaningful rituals and, as much as we love to have fun, we also like giving back to the land by planting trees. We also passionately believe in the power of TRANSFORMATION THROUGH PARTICIPATION. Welcome to the next evolution of our ongoing journey! For ticket discounts, other important updates and to announce your own offering(s), join our Summer Solstice Community on WhatsApp! https://chat.whatsapp.com/IV6TpYZkPdJ7GJXL3kkQpX HOW WE ROLL At our family-friendly event, alcohol, other drugs and psychedelic stimulants are not welcome. Nor are bad attitudes and big egos. We love to drum, to dance and to make merry, as well as strike a good balance between sound and silence. And we collectively co-create a safe space and container for everyone, including those who are sensitive. We encourage a healthy, balanced lifestyle featuring all the tools at our disposal (yoga, breathwork, sound journeys, sweat lodges, and so forth…). Our musicians, DJs and drummers have their glory moments, but not to the detriment of a good night’s rest for all. We encourage each participant to make the most of an amazing environment where you can rest, relax and resource yourself from nature… while having loads of fun into the bargain! We also favour intimacy, quality over quantity, and spaciousness rather than frenetic activity. And we collectively build a spirit of community by encouraging everyone to trade goods at our daily Talent Market. If you would like to trade more formally in our Trading Emporium, please reach out to book your stall. WHAT ARE TALENTS? It’s a mechanism for trading your skills or goods with others. It stems from the global Community Exchange Talent System and makes the event more accessible to those who are financially challenged and may not have much hard cash to spend. The ethos of the event is for all those who attend it to experience a sense of financial buoyancy. In order to achieve this, we highly recommend you engage with the Talent System and immerse yourself in the experience. It’s easy and effective – all the more so if you show up and honour yourself! To register for your personal exchange number, go here: www.community-exchange.org/home/ VOLUNTEERING Each volunteer receives a free ticket, at least one yummy vegetarian meal per day, plus a cash donation (provided they stay till the end). There are only 16 places available on the team, so to avoid disappointment fill in your application form soonest. Go here: http://bit.ly/4ngv9yr DATES Arrival: from 2pm on Monday, 14 December (If you want to arrive earlier, please purchase your Early Arrivals Pass via the Well-Being Sanctuary website: ) Self-sufficient camping (or glamping): Tuesday, 15 December We encourage you to participate in a Sweat Lodge on this day, to help you ground yourself after a busy year. Or go for a walk & a swim! Wednesday, 16 December to 10am on Wednesday, 23 December Seven days of immersive community celebration FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQs) Please go here: https://bit.ly/4tvCa01 TICKETING POLICY We care for the Well-Being Sanctuary environment and are committed to managing the impact of our footprint on the land. Thus, ticket sales are limited to a maximum of 600. We encourage you to immerse yourself in the community experience, and do not sell day passes as we do not want the nuisance factor of curious spectators dropping in. Importantly, please note: we do not sell tickets at the gate! And we have a NO REFUNDS policy. If, due to unforeseen circumstances you cannot attend the event, you may sell your ticket to a friend – on condition that you notify us in advance of the arrangement. TICKET CATEGORIES AND PRICES TRIBE LOYALTY TICKET FOR ADULTS R899 (or R99.88 per day) Available from 6 May to 30 May (70 tickets – first come, first served, no exceptions!) STANDARD TICKET FOR ADULTS R1,999 (or R222,11 per day) Available once the Tribe Loyalty Tickets are sold out, and until 30 September (limited number of tickets for sale) LATE RISER TICKET FOR ADULTS R2,999 (or R333,22 per day) Available from 1 October to 23 December (limited number of tickets for sale) STANDARD TICKET FOR KIDS (ages 6 to 16) R699 (or R77,66 per day; ages 1 to 5 free entry) Available from 6 May to 23 December STANDARD FAMILY TICKET (2 Adults, 2 Kids ages 6 to 16) R4,299 (or R477,66 per day; 20% reduction compared to standard tickets) Available from 1 June to 23 December WEEKEND PASS FOR ADULTS (18 to 21 Dec; 4 days, 5 nights) R1,999 (or R499,75 per day) Available from 9 December to 21 December MOTORISED CAMPING PASS (camping next to or on top of your vehicle in our designated vehicle camping zones; valid for the entire event) R299 (or R33,22 per day) Available from 6 May to 23 December EARLY ARRIVALS PASS (valid on 12 & 13 December) R799 (irrespective of your arrival date) Available from 6 May to 23 December GLAMPING Deluxe Glamping is available – it sells out fast, so first come first served! Preference is given to those attending for more than three days. Whether you prefer a shady spot or basking in the sun, our glamping village offers an array of tents with carpeted floors, pillows, and soft quality bedding. Our 5m Bell tents are spacious enough to stand up in, allowing you to move freely and comfortably. From your tent, enjoy the rolling green of lush meadows, and the beauty of the fairy forest. You also have the option to book one of our seven, absolutely stunning, fully furnished Yurts. Positioned along the ridge overlooking Swartvlei Lake, they offer the convenience of having your own en suite bathroom with gas-heated shower. With tracks hugging the rugged coastline and views only seen on postcards, this ride is designed for the intermediate cyclist looking for an adventure without having to spend hours training every day. The daily distances range from 40-70 kms and will traverse the mountains, plantations and coastline adjacent to the Village. Whether you’re a mountain-biking maestro or just getting started, there’s a spot for you to join and share the thrill of a stage race experience. Mountain bikes and eBikes are welcome; there’s something for riders of all ages and skill levels. Thrilling rides, relaxing walks, an extraordinary setting and non stop pampering. Whether you’re on the trail or kicking back in the Race Village, these are the ingredients for an unforgettable weekend. Join us for a weekend of mountain-biking and family fun. Enter the #StormsRiverTraverse through the app to qualify for your tier level discount. DRYLAND REWARDS PROGRAM Many of our loyal supporters take part in multiple Dryland events in a calendar year and often across different disciplines. Athletes stand the chance to qualify for between 5% and 60% value back on their event entries, with the higher tiers qualifying for even more benefits. LOYALTY WILL BE REWARDED Visit www.drylandrewards.co.za The level of value back offered is determined by the rider/runner’s qualifying tier level. The opening tier levels are determined by the number of events the participant successfully completed during the last complete run of events. RECENT NEWS SEE NEWS Sunshine and Good Times in the Tsitsikamma at the Glacier Storms River Traverse Good times are certainly synonymous with the Glacier Storms River Traverse. Sunshine… not as much. Not subscribed yet? Sign up below for your free weekly garden route event guide Subscribe Email sent! Check your inbox to complete your signup. No spam. Unsubscribe anytime. Mossel Bay Tanja Storm: Ballads and Blues Tanja Storm performs an evening of ballads and blues with guest Blackie Swart at this Little Brak River music venue. Date:  Wednesday 7 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  Blou Kombuis, 2nd Avenue, Little Brak River, Mossel Bay Moss March A community walk with purpose on the Hartenbos seafront, part of the Mossel Bay Sport and Recreation Festival. Entry is free; walkers are asked to bring tinned or non-perishable food and socks for those in need. Strongman and powerlifting competitions follow at the same venue. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  07:00 to 09:00 Venue:  Hartenbos Seefront, 156 Paardekraal Avenue, Hartenbos, Mossel Bay Garden Route Armwrestling Tournament A double-elimination showdown open to first-timers and seasoned pullers alike. Entry is R100 for one arm or R150 for both, and spectator tickets cost R100. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  Registration and weigh-ins from 08:30, tournament from 10:00 Venue:  Mooiuitsig Restaurant, Brinkley's River Village, 1 Old George Road, Klein Brak River, Mossel Bay Misty Valley Oktoberfest The farm's second Oktoberfest runs every Saturday in October with craft beer, food and live music. Entrance is free and the day is cashless. Date:  Saturday 10 October and Saturday 17 October Time:  09:00 to 18:00 Venue:  Misty Valley Farm, R328, Brandwacht, Mossel Bay Jo Black Live at ReedValley An evening of Afrikaans music from Jo Black on the wine estate, with ReedValley wines and food on sale. Tickets start at R220. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  20:00 Venue:  ReedValley Farm, R327, Mossel Bay Magnificent Movie Music Carpe Musicam brings its programme of orchestral and choral film favourites to the Town Hall for a 90-minute Sunday afternoon concert, with violinist Marie-Jean Kotzé as soloist. Tickets cost R180 for adults and R60 for scholars from carpemusicam.co.za. Date:  Sunday 11 October Time:  15:30 Venue:  Mossel Bay Town Hall, 101 Marsh Street, Mossel Bay Song Sung Blue at The Blue Shed Open Plan Pictures screens Song Sung Blue, the story of two down-on-their-luck performers who form a Neil Diamond tribute act, as part of its spring movie series. Tickets start at R100. Date:  Friday 16 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  The Blue Shed, 33 Bland Street, Mossel Bay Topper Nationals Mossel Bay Sailing Club and the Skipper Foundation host the national championship for the Topper dinghy class. Spectators are welcome on the beach to watch young sailors race in the bay. Date:  Saturday 17 October and Sunday 18 October Time:  10:00 to 17:00 Venue:  Santos Beach, Santos Road, Mossel Bay George Carpe Musicam: Magnificent Movie Music The Carpe Musicam Concert Orchestra and Choir play a dozen film themes spanning eight decades, from The Sound of Music to The Mission and The Mask of Zorro, with violinist Marie-Jean Kotzé as soloist. Tickets cost R180 for adults and R60 for scholars, with limited sales at the door. Date:  Friday 9 October Time:  19:00 Venue:  Laerskool George-Suid, corner of Meade and Laing Streets, George MRC Rugby Expo Two days of senior men's club rugby, under-19 and under-13 schoolboy rugby, senior ladies' netball and chess, with food vendors, a cash bar and live entertainment. Entry is R50 for adults. Date:  Saturday 10 October and Sunday 11 October Time:  From 09:00 Venue:  Pacaltsdorp Sportgronde, 66 Olympic Street, Pacaltsdorp, George Espectáculo Marlise's School of Spanish Dance presents an evening of Spanish dance. Tickets cost R150 through Webtickets. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  18:30 Venue:  Market Community Theatre, George Sedgefield Country Sokkie Evening at La Bosca Country music and sokkie dancing in the countryside, with a Best Dressed Country Couple competition. The restaurant serves Portuguese and Italian dishes from noon. Tickets cost R80 for adults and R40 for children aged 6 to 12. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  19:00 to 23:00 Venue:  La Bosca, Luna Verde Farm, Barrington Road, Sedgefield Pink Walk for Breast Cancer Awareness A free 4.5 km community walk in pink, with prizes for the best dressed. Donations go to Hospice Sedgefield. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  08:30 Venue:  Engen Garage, Sedgefield Garden Route Kite Festival The tenth RE/MAX Garden Route Kite Festival brings kite flyers and makers from nine countries to Sedgefield. Bring a kite, make one on the day or buy one there. Food stalls, coffee and family entertainment run all day, and entry is free. Date:  Sunday 18 October Time:  09:30 to 15:30 Venue:  Scarab Village, Sedgefield Knysna Schalk Bezuidenhout: Hey Hey Divorce Schalk Bezuidenhout's stand-up show about his own divorce, which he says is cheaper than therapy. Tickets cost R300 with unreserved seating, and doors open at 19:00. Date:  Tuesday 20 October Time:  20:00 Venue:  Simola Hotel Country Club and Spa, Knysna Plettenberg Bay Blithe Spirit The Bitou Amateur Theatrical Society stages Noël Coward's ghost comedy, directed and designed by David Hall-Green. Tuesday is the gala opening, with doors at 18:30 and complimentary wine and cheese. Tickets cost R350 from Barney's Kiosk or Quicket. Date:  Tuesday 6 October to Saturday 10 October Time:  19:30 Venue:  St Peter's Church, Plettenberg Bay Bekkersdal Bachelors and Blunders A one-man evening of Herman Charles Bosman's Oom Schalk Lourens stories, told with dry Groot Marico humour. Tickets are sold through Quicket. Date:  Tuesday 6 October Time:  19:30 Venue:  The White House Theatre, 6 Crescent Street, Plettenberg Bay Plett Games A family festival hosted by Greenwood Bay College. Teams of three to five, or individuals, work through twelve challenges, from gumboot throwing and golf chipping to slow cycling and paper plane contests. The Bitou River Band plays live, with sourdough pizza, a beer garden, a tea garden and children's play areas. Tickets cost R30 to R150. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  10:00 to 17:00 Venue:  Greenwood Bay College, Piesang Valley Road, Plettenberg Bay Oudtshoorn Optimum Meiringspoort Half Marathon The 32nd edition of this much-loved road race offers 21.1 km and 12.5 km distances. After flood damage, runners are now transported out on the Uniondale road (R341) for a run back into De Rust. Entries are sold out, and spectators can catch the finish at the church grounds. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  12.5 km starts 07:00, 21.1 km starts 07:15 Venue:  Finish at the NG Church grounds, De Rust, near Oudtshoorn Hemelruim: Music Under the Stars A new open-air concert from the KKNK, billed as a desert disco under the Klein Karoo sky. Spoegwolf, Tasché and Oudtshoorn's own Noemwoord share the stage. The concert has moved to a new venue, Surval Boutique Olive Estate. Tickets cost R295 through Computicket, and children aged 7 to 13 pay R100 at the gate. Date:  Saturday 10 October Time:  Gates open at 17:00, music from 18:00 Venue:  Surval Boutique Olive Estate, R328, Oudtshoorn Klein Karoo Dust 4 Glory Challenge An obstacle course race with climbing, crawling, water and mud, part of the OFSA National Series. Distances range from a 1 to 2 km Mini for ages 3 to 10 up to the 12 km Pro with more than 20 obstacles. Entries cost R150 to R550 and are limited. Date:  Saturday 17 October Time:  Registration 06:00 to 08:00; Medium at 08:00, Pro at 09:00, junior races at 12:00 Venue:  Wilgewandel Holiday Farm, 2 km from the Cango Caves, Oudtshoorn That’s a wrap! If this edition gave you some good ideas, please share it with a friend or neighbour. Word of mouth is how we grow, and your support keeps us tracking the best of the Garden Route. Hit the share button below - thanks for reading. Bar & Kitchen – Wilderness Beach House Backpackers Home Accommodation Bar & Kitchen Menu Activities Blog Gallery Contact Book Now Book Now Bar & Kitchen Beach House Bar & Kitchen is the pub and wood-fired pizza kitchen at Beach House Wilderness Backpackers, on the hillside above Wilderness Beach on the Garden Route. It is a small bar with a big view: a deck looking straight out over the Indian Ocean, about 100 metres from the sand. You do not have to be staying with us to eat here. Most nights the room is a mix of guests, locals and people who pulled off the N2 and stayed longer than they planned. Wood-fired oven from 11:00 daily Walk-in, no reservations Ocean-view deck Dogs welcome on the deck Free parking 4.5 stars from 791 Google reviews Pizzas go into the wood-fired oven from 11:00 daily. Wood-fired pizza in Wilderness The oven is the centre of the kitchen and it is a proper wood-fired one, not a pizza tray in a domestic oven. The pizza list starts with a vegetarian garlic and herb focaccia at R75 and a garlic, herb and feta focaccia at R100, then ten named pizzas from R110 to R175, from The Backpacker (a margherita) to The Vic Bay (bacon, ham and sausage). Extra toppings are R25 for avo, bacon, chicken, feta, ham, mushroom or sausage, and R15 for banana, green pepper, onion, pineapple or tomatoes. The Backpacker and The Milkwood (mushroom, green pepper, caramelised onion and tomato) have no meat toppings. Beyond pizza the kitchen does burgers, wraps, salads, sarmies, tapas and a breakfast list, with cake and chocolate brownies for dessert and daily desserts on display at the bar. You can read the full Bar & Kitchen menu with prices , which is the same list the kitchen works from. The bar The bar runs local and imported beer by the dumpie and the quart, cider, wine by the glass and the bottle, spirits, a short cocktail list and a full alcohol-free range. There is George Brewery on tap. Corkage is R45 if you bring your own wine. There is a pool table, and the deck is where most people end up at sunset. Live music, open mic and pool nights Live acts play the deck every Sunday from 15:00 to 18:00. Open mic runs every Thursday from 18:00 to 22:00 with One Two Sound Solutions, and Friday is pool and darts from 18:00. Entry is free unless a show is specifically ticketed. See what is on at Beach House for the dated gig list. Where to find us We are on Western Road in Wilderness, Western Cape, walkable from the village centre and roughly 15 km east of George and 20 km west of Sedgefield on the N2. Parking is free, with limited space on site and street parking that is usually easy outside a busy Saturday evening. It is about a two minute walk down to the beach. Get in touch on WhatsApp or open us in Google Maps . Eating your way around the village? We keep a local guide to restaurants in Wilderness that covers more than just our own kitchen. Stay the night The bar and the backpackers are the same property, so you can eat, catch a set and walk to your bed. See our rooms and rates , from ocean-view dorm beds to en-suite rooms and garden tents. Check availability Frequently asked questions What time does the kitchen open at Beach House Bar and Kitchen? The wood-fired oven runs from 11:00 daily, which is when pizza starts coming out. Bar and kitchen service beyond that shifts with the season and the day of the week, and our Sunday live music runs 15:00 to 18:00 with Thursday open mic from 18:00 to 22:00. If you are travelling specifically to eat with us, send a quick WhatsApp to 071 495 1814 and we will tell you what is running that day. Do I need to book a table? No. The Bar and Kitchen is walk-in only and we do not hold tables. On a busy evening, and particularly on a Sunday when there is live music, arrive before sunset if you want a seat on the deck. On quieter weeknights you can usually walk in late and still find a spot. Accommodation is different and does get booked up in advance. Do you have vegetarian options? Yes, and they are on the standing menu rather than a special request. The garlic and herb focaccia is vegetarian, The Backpacker (a margherita) and The Milkwood pizzas have no meat toppings, and there is a falafel platter, a falafel wrap, a Greek salad, and hummus or baba ghanoush as sides. For any other dietary requirement, ask at the bar. Can non-guests eat at Beach House? Yes. You do not need to be staying with us. The bar and kitchen are open to the public and a good share of the room on any given night is locals and day visitors. There is free parking on site and on the street, and we are an easy walk from Wilderness village. Are dogs allowed? Friendly dogs are welcome on the deck, which is where most people eat anyway. Please keep them with you and under control, especially on live music nights when the deck gets busy. If you are bringing a dog and staying the night as well, mention it when you book so we can put you somewhere sensible. Wilderness Backpackers on the Garden Route. 100 metres from the ocean. Situated just outside of Wilderness towards Sedgefield, this unique village offers visitors a delightful blend of shopping, dining, and outdoor activities in a picturesque setting. Visitors can explore a variety of artisanal shops and boutiques showcasing locally made crafts, gifts, and souvenirs. From handcrafted jewelry and pottery to organic skincare products and African art, there’s something to suit every taste and interest. After browsing the shops, guests can indulge in a culinary adventure at one of the village’s charming eateries. From cozy cafes serving up freshly brewed coffee and homemade treats to gourmet restaurants offering innovative cuisine made with locally sourced ingredients, Timberlake Village promises a diverse and delicious dining experience. For those seeking outdoor adventure, Timberlake Village is the home of Acrobranch, an aerial obstacle course through the trees. The village also offers an outdoor playground for children. With its quaint charm, vibrant atmosphere, and stunning natural surroundings, Timberlake Village invites visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty and creativity of South Africa’s Garden Route. Whether shopping, dining, or exploring the great outdoors, there’s something for everyone to enjoy at this enchanting destination. With The Billy Joel Experience he won a prestigious award on national television ( The Tribute: Battle of the Bands – SBS6) and has sold out leading theatres all across the Netherlands. After two sold-out tours in 2024 and 2025, Alexander returns to South Africa this December for a brand new series of concerts. Once again he performs with his own South African band, proudly named The Lords of Longstreet – a playful nod to Joel’s original group, The Lords of 52nd Street . Expect an unforgettable evening filled with Billy Joel’s timeless hits, performed with passion, authenticity and world-class musicianship. From Piano Man to New York State of Mind and beyond – this is a show that will make you sing along, dance, and rediscover the genius of one of the greatest songwriters of all time. Alexander has shared the stage with Billy Joel’s legendary band members Richie Cannata (saxophone) and Liberty DeVitto (drums) – both of whom gave him their personal “stamp of approval” . Now South African audiences can experience the magic of his show live. *Don’t miss this chance – join Alexander Broussard & The Lords of Longstreet for a spectacular celebration of the music of Billy Joel. Hierdie besondere produksie neem gehore op ’n diep persoonlike en musikale reis deur meer as twee dekades se liedjies, stories en groei. Van die rou eerlikheid van Melkstraat Confessions , die ikoniese debuutalbum wat Blohm as ’n unieke stem in Afrikaanse musiek gevestig het, tot by sy nuutste en mees reflektiewe werk, Tot daar waar die lig is , word sy loopbaan met nuwe diepte en betekenis gevier. In hierdie intieme vertoning verweef Blohm sy musiek met sy lewensverhaal. Met treffers, diep snitte en vars materiaal bring hy die volle spektrum van sy kunstenaarskap na die verhoog. Elke lied dra ’n storie, van liefde, verlies en verlange tot soeke, hoop en lig. At De Vette Mossel (The Fat Mussel) , we believe in more than just a meal. Experience the ambience and unwind in front of a crackling bonfire with a glass of the finest in hand – right there on the beach!
